recent.title: The Poet Empress
recent.author: Shen Tao
recent.review: i finished this a few days ago and i STILL don't think i've fully recovered. this was an immediate five star read , possibly even six , because apparently i've developed a habit of falling in love with books that leave me completely hollow. and this one... yeah. this book sank its blades into me and absolutely REFUSED to let go. the funniest part is that i was actually TERRIFIED to pick this up. after dnfing the unicorn hunters , seeing "political fantasy" in the tags was enough to make me question whether i'd even enjoy this. my illumicrate copy had been sitting on my shelf for MONTHS until i randomly came across a few tiktoks calling it one of the best books of the year and decided to give it a chance. ON HALLOWEEKEND OF ALL TIMES. i genuinely thought there was no way i'd be finishing this anytime soon because i had SO much going on , between going out with friends , celebrating halloween and everything else i had planned. reading was probably the last thing i expected to have time for. WELL... none of that mattered because i was hooked from the very first chapter and somehow managed to read almost 300 pages on friday alone before finishing the rest on halloween. TWO DAYS. during one of the busiest weekends i've had in a while. i genuinely could NOT put this thing down. the court politics ended up being one of my FAVORITE parts of this entire book which is actually hilarious considering how much i was dreading them. the tension , the calculated power plays , the constant feeling that one wrong move could completely ruin someone. I LOVED IT ALL. everyone wants a piece of power and absolutely nobody is above doing whatever it takes to get it. every conversation felt like someone was inches away from walking into a trap and i was eating up every second of it. and TERREN... oh my god. here's someone who appears so cold , cruel and almost irredeemable on the outside , but the more you learn about him , the more you realize just how badly the very system he was born into failed him. he's such a morally gray character and i LOVE that about him. it doesn't excuse everything he's done , but damn does it make his character so much more heartbreaking. he was exploited by the very people that were supposed to protect him , right until the very end. how am i NOT supposed to sympathize with him after everything he's been through ?? genuinely one of the best MMCs i've read about in a LONG time. WEI THOUGH. i absolutely ADORE her. it's been so long since i've read a book where i can confidently say that i loved BOTH of the main characters this much. like genuinely , i don't think there's a single thing i'd change about either of them. their complexity , their development , the decisions they make and everything they have to endure... i just wanted to reach into the pages and give them both a hug. and the two of them together ?? perfect for each other in another life , FOR REAL. i'm actually going to cry again if i think about this for too long. i read and watch a LOT of horror , and i think i've become pretty desensitized to disturbing things at this point. especially with everything happening in the world right now , where we're constantly exposed to increasingly horrific things that people are capable of doing to each other. sometimes even the most disturbing things in fiction barely faze me anymore , which is why i've always said that if a book manages to make me emotional or even tear up , it's immediately entering my six star territory. AND THIS BOOK DID SO MUCH WORSE. i was literally sitting there begging for things to turn out okay because i could NOT handle watching these characters suffer anymore. and of course , every time i thought things couldn't possibly get more devastating , something else would happen and i'd be right back to questioning why i willingly put myself through this. that ending !! i don't even know whether to call it happy or sad. bittersweet is probably the closest i'll ever get because it somehow managed to leave me feeling relieved and absolutely HEARTBROKEN at the same time. i could literally write an entire essay about how much i love this book and STILL not have enough words to explain it. the characters , the writing , the storytelling... it all came together so beautifully and i honestly don't think i could've asked for more. and the fact that this is a DEBUT is actually INSANE to me. shen tao , you've absolutely outdone yourself because WHAT A BOOK. i'm so glad i finally picked this up after putting it off for so long because this was easily one of the best reading decisions i've made all year. (six stars in my heart because five is simply NOT enough)

recent.title: What Feeds Below
recent.author: Tatiana Schlote-Bonne
recent.review: the void is a living nightmare and somehow i STILL wanted to explore every inch of it. WHAT IS WRONG WITH ME ? 😭 i think the void itself is what made this book so memorable. it’s such a horrifying yet fascinating place , and i was obsessed with how vividly it was described. everything feels so alive and thriving in a way , from the monstrous creatures to the most unassuming little organisms that can kill you before you even realise you’re in danger. the cryptids and mutations only made it all the more unsettling. it genuinely felt like stepping into a fever dream , and i loved every second of it. and THE BODY HORROR ??? as a horror fan , i was VERY happy with how brutal some of the imagery got. the descriptions did not hold back , and i was absolutely LIVING for every horrifying detail. pair that with the pacing , where practically every chapter has SOMETHING happening , and you’ve got yourself an incredibly addictive little horror read. i also really loved our main character and her view on life. even though she definitely had her flaws , i thought she showed so much character development by the end. in a world where practically everything is trying to kill you , she’s looking at these horrifying organisms and wondering how she could turn them into medicine. there’s something so endearing about someone who can find the potential for healing in a place filled with so much death. what surprised me too was how much the story had to say about love and validation , and the lengths we’re willing to go to feel wanted. there’s this underlying question of what happens when you become so attached to someone that you start losing yourself in them. where do you draw the line between loving someone and needing them to the point where you can’t exist outside their shadow ? i thought that was a really interesting layer beneath all the chaos. now , the reason this isn’t quite a perfect read for me is the ending. while i found it sad and wished things could’ve turned out differently , the main twist was unfortunately something i’d already pieced together. some of the clues scattered throughout the story weren’t exactly subtle , so i never got that HOLY SHIT WHAT JUST HAPPENED moment i was hoping for. there’s also one particular detail about how quickly things escalated towards the end with the mutations that i'm still a little confused about. but none of that took away from how much i enjoyed the overall experience. i’m SO glad i managed to squeeze this into the final week of october despite being swamped with internship work. it was literally the perfect way to close out spooky reading month... although let’s be real , october ending is NOT going to stop me from reading horror well into november and december. SO glad i picked this up to close out my october. i’ll definitely be keeping an eye on whatever this author writes next !
